title: Northern Rhône
description: Steep granite slopes above the Rhône, home of Syrah and Viognier.
L: The northern Rhône runs about 60 km along the Rhône river, from Vienne, south of Lyon, to Valence. Vineyards cling to steep slopes on both banks, mostly granite and schist, often on terraces held by dry-stone walls, called chaillées. It's small: about 5% of all Rhône wine.

The climate is continental, cooler than the south, with the Mistral wind blowing down the valley. Steep, south and south-east facing slopes catch the sun and drain cold air, letting Syrah ripen this far north. Terraces stop soil erosion. Work is by hand, sometimes with winches, making the wines costly.
Why do northern Rhône vineyards use terraces?
To hold soil on steep slopes
Terraces prevent erosion and make work possible.

Vines have grown here since Roman times; Vienne was an important Roman city, and its wine was praised by Pliny. Hermitage takes its name from a 13th century knight, Gaspard de Stérimberg, who, legend says, lived there as a hermit after the Crusades.
Roman vines; the hermit of Hermitage
The northern Rhône makes most of the Rhône's wine.
Not true. It makes about 5%; the south makes over 90%.
The northern Rhône runs 60 km on steep granite slopes
Steep, sunny slopes ripen Syrah in a continental climate
It's small, about 5% of Rhône wine

Syrah is the only red grape allowed in the northern Rhône. It gives deep, peppery wines with blackberry, violet, olive and smoked meat. Some appellations let small amounts of white grapes be co-fermented with it: up to 20% Viognier in Côte-Rôtie, 15% Marsanne and Roussanne in Hermitage, though most use much less.

Viognier makes Condrieu and Château-Grillet: rich, apricot and violet. Marsanne and Roussanne make white Hermitage, Crozes-Hermitage, Saint-Joseph and Saint-Péray, where they also make sparkling wine. Marsanne gives body; Roussanne gives aroma and freshness.
Match each grape to its main use.
The northern Rhône has a short grape list.
Co-fermenting a little Viognier with Syrah helps fix colour and adds a floral lift. In Côte-Rôtie, it's typically 2 to 5%.
Which is the only red grape allowed in the northern Rhône?
Syrah is the northern Rhône's only red grape
Viognier makes Condrieu; Marsanne and Roussanne white Hermitage
Small amounts of white grapes can be co-fermented with Syrah

Côte-Rôtie, the roasted slope, lies at the northern end, on very steep schist slopes facing south-east. Its two famous slopes are the Côte Brune, darker, more structured, and the Côte Blonde, lighter, more perfumed. Wines are elegant, floral and peppery. Guigal's single-vineyard La Mouline, La Landonne and La Turque made it famous.

Hermitage is a single, south-facing granite hill above Tain-l'Hermitage. Its reds are powerful, tannic and long-lived, among France's greatest. About a quarter is white, mostly Marsanne, also long-lived. Famous producers include Chapoutier, Jaboulet, with La Chapelle, and Jean-Louis Chave. In the 19th century, Bordeaux was sometimes hermitagé, strengthened with it.
A single hill, powerful and long-lived
What are the Côte Brune and Côte Blonde?
Brune is darker and firmer; Blonde lighter and perfumed.

Cornas makes dark, rustic, powerful Syrah on granite. Saint-Joseph, a long strip on the west bank, makes lighter, fruitier reds. Crozes-Hermitage, the largest appellation, on flatter land around Hermitage, offers good value. Condrieu and Château-Grillet make Viognier; Saint-Péray, whites and sparkling.
Gigondas is in the southern Rhône.
Côte-Rôtie is elegant, on Brune and Blonde slopes
Hermitage is a powerful, long-lived single hill
Cornas, Saint-Joseph and Crozes complete the reds
Reading the northern Rhône and eating with it
Pair Syrah and Viognier with food

Labels name the appellation, like Côte-Rôtie or Crozes-Hermitage, the producer and sometimes a lieu-dit, a named vineyard. Grapes aren't usually named, but every red is Syrah. Négociants like Guigal, Chapoutier and Jaboulet are important, alongside small domaines.

Northern Rhône Syrah suits lamb with herbs and black pepper, game, duck and grilled beef; its pepper echoes peppercorn sauces. Condrieu suits lobster, crab and dishes with apricot or mild spice. White Hermitage suits rich fish and truffles. Serve reds at 16 to 18 degrees; decant young Hermitage and Cornas.
Which dish suits a Cornas or Hermitage?
Rich game and pepper suit Syrah's power and spice.
Crozes-Hermitage and Saint-Joseph from good producers offer a taste of northern Rhône Syrah at a fraction of Hermitage prices.
Great Hermitage can age for decades.
Labels name the appellation; reds are Syrah
Syrah suits lamb, game and peppercorn sauce
Hermitage and Cornas benefit from decanting and age

Up to 20%, though most use much less.

Not true. Syrah is the only red grape there.
The north is steep, not flat.
For its sun-baked, south-east facing slopes.
